sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with treatment-resistant depression who cannot tolerate medication.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.
Eligibility Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
1. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
2. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 4 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
3. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of major depressive disorder.
4. A psychiatric evaluation has confirmed the diagnosis.
Limitations
The following limitations apply:
- Treatment delivered with devices not cleared for depression is not covered.
- Maintenance treatment after remission is not covered.
Required Testing
Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 18 months before the initial treatment session must be available. Objective findings that confirm major depressive disorder must be documented by the treating practitioner.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in psychiatry. Facilities furnishing transcranial magnetic stimulation must maintain written protocols for emergency response.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
A course of treatment is limited to 30 sessions over 6 weeks.
Documentation Requirements
The following documentation must be available upon request:
The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about transcranial magnetic stimulation. Results of a standardized depression rating scale relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record. The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for transcranial magnetic stimulation from the treating practitioner.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
1. F32.2 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
2. F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate
3. F33.2 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent severe without psychotic features
4. F33.9 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, unspecified

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
- Report one unit of service for each treatment session furnished.
- Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.
- Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the treatment session was furnished.
- The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim.

sections.heading: Applicability
sections.text: This policy applies to claims with dates of service on or after 09/01/2023.

sections.text:

- Example Journal of Psychiatry. Outcomes of transcranial magnetic stimulation in older adults. 2016.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.
Medical Necessity Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 2 adequate trials of antidepressant medication. The beneficiary has no implanted metallic device near the treatment coil.
Limitations
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered. Simultaneous treatment with electroconvulsive therapy is not covered.
Required Testing
The following clinical evidence is required:
Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 6 months before the initial treatment session must be available. A baseline result from a standardized depression rating scale must be recorded before the initial treatment session.
Provider Qualifications
The following qualifications apply:
1. Facilities furnishing transcranial magnetic stimulation must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
2. Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform transcranial magnetic stimulation under state law.
3. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
A course of treatment is limited to 30 sessions over 7 weeks.
Documentation Requirements
The following documentation must be available upon request:
1. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment session.
2. Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each treatment session.
3. The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about transcranial magnetic stimulation.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for transcranial magnetic stimulation:
- F32.2 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
- F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate
- F33.2 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent severe without psychotic features
- F33.9 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, unspecified

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
- Report the date of the initial treatment session on the claim.
- Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.
- Telehealth delivery of transcranial magnetic stimulation is not separately billable under this policy.
- Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the treatment session was furnished.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies. Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence. Evidence for benefit is strongest when transcranial magnetic stimulation is combined with ongoing medical management.

sections.text:
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with treatment-resistant depression who cannot tolerate medication.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
sections.text:
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
The beneficiary is not at acute risk of suicide requiring inpatient care. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 3 adequate trials of antidepressant medication. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of major depressive disorder.

sections.heading: Non-Covered Services
sections.text:
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is not covered for beneficiaries with a seizure disorder. Maintenance treatment after remission is not covered.

sections.heading: Frequency and Duration
sections.text:
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
A course of treatment is limited to 36 sessions over 9 weeks.

sections.heading: Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
sections.text:
The following clinical evidence is required:
- Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 12 months before the initial treatment session must be available.
- Objective findings that confirm major depressive disorder must be documented by the treating practitioner.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
sections.text:
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each treatment session. The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity. A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before transcranial magnetic stimulation begins. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment session.

sections.heading: Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
sections.text:
1. The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare.
2. Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform transcranial magnetic stimulation under state law.
3. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for transcranial magnetic stimulation:
1. F32.1 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
2. F32.2 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
3. F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate
4. F33.9 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, unspecified

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
Claims for transcranial magnetic stimulation furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line. Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected. Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Published studies report improvements in depression rating scale scores among beneficiaries receiving transcranial magnetic stimulation. Evidence for benefit is strongest when transcranial magnetic stimulation is combined with ongoing medical management.

sections.heading: Applicability
sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 10/01/2021.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
This section describes the indications for which hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered.
1. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with decompression illness.
2. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with diabetic lower extremity wounds.
3. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with osteoradionecrosis.
Patient Selection Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
- The wound is classified as Wagner grade 4 or higher.
- The wound has failed to respond to standard wound therapy for at least 30 days.
- The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
- The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
Limitations
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for beneficiaries with untreated pneumothorax.
- Treatment continued without measurable signs of healing after 30 days is not covered.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The following qualifications apply:
- The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare.
- The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in hyperbaric oxygen therapy.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Utilization Guidelines
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is limited to 40 treatments within a 60-day period.
Documentation Requirements
The following documentation must be available upon request:
- A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before hyperbaric oxygen therapy begins.
- The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.
- The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about hyperbaric oxygen therapy.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:

- E11.621 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
- M27.8 - Other specified diseases of jaws
- T58.01XA - Toxic effect of carbon monoxide from motor vehicle exhaust, accidental (unintentional), initial encounter
- T70.3XXA - Caisson disease [decompression sickness], initial encounter

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
Telehealth delivery of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not separately billable under this policy. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the treatment was furnished.

sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when hyperbaric oxygen therapy is combined with ongoing medical management. Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence.

sections.heading: Implementation
sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 04/01/2024.

Transcranial magnetic stimulation is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.

2. Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.

4. Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder.

The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of major depressive disorder. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 2 adequate trials of antidepressant medication. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.

The following limitations apply:
1. Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered.
2. Simultaneous treatment with electroconvulsive therapy is not covered.
3. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is not covered for beneficiaries with a seizure disorder.
Provider Qualifications
The following qualifications apply:
Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for major depressive disorder. - A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before transcranial magnetic stimulation begins.
- The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for transcranial magnetic stimulation from the treating practitioner.
- The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about transcranial magnetic stimulation.
- Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each treatment session.

sections.heading: Indications for Coverage
sections.text:
This section describes the indications for which bone mass measurement may be covered.
1. Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism.
2. Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries receiving long-term glucocorticoid therapy.
3. Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries being monitored on an FDA-approved osteoporosis medication.

sections.heading: Patient Selection Criteria
sections.text:
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
The beneficiary is at least 65 years of age. Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement. The ordering practitioner is treating the beneficiary for a condition that affects bone density.

sections.heading: Limitations and Exclusions
sections.text:
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
- Vertebral fracture assessment billed alone without a qualifying indication is not covered.
- Testing more often than the frequency limit is not covered without documented medical necessity.
- Bone mass measurement is not covered for beneficiaries without a qualifying risk factor.

sections.heading: Utilization Guidelines
sections.text: Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 12 months.

sections.heading: Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
sections.text:
1. Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry obtained within 3 months before the initial scan must be available.
2. A baseline result from dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry must be recorded before the initial scan.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements
sections.text:
The following documentation must be available upon request:
- When bone mass measurement continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.
- The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.
- Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each scan.
- The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for bone mass measurement from the treating practitioner.

sections.heading: Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
sections.text:
The following qualifications apply:
The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in bone mass measurement. Facilities furnishing bone mass measurement must maintain written protocols for emergency response. Staff furnishing bone mass measurement must hold current basic life support certification. Bone mass measurement must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for bone mass measurement:
1. E28.310 - Symptomatic premature menopause
2. M81.0 - Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
3. Z87.310 - Personal history of (healed) osteoporosis fracture

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
1. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the scan was furnished.
2. Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.
3. The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim.

sections.text: Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence. The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Covered Indications
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with treatment-resistant depression who cannot tolerate medication.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.
Eligibility Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
The beneficiary has not responded to at least 4 adequate trials of antidepressant medication. A psychiatric evaluation has confirmed the diagnosis. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period. The beneficiary is not at acute risk of suicide requiring inpatient care.
Limitations and Exclusions
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
Treatment delivered with devices not cleared for depression is not covered. Maintenance treatment after remission is not covered.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The following qualifications apply:
1. Facilities furnishing transcranial magnetic stimulation must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
2. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for major depressive disorder.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Utilization Guidelines
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
A course of treatment is limited to 30 sessions over 7 weeks.
Documentation Requirements
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
1. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment session.
2. The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for transcranial magnetic stimulation from the treating practitioner.
3. The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about transcranial magnetic stimulation.
4. A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before transcranial magnetic stimulation begins.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for transcranial magnetic stimulation:
1. F32.1 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
2. F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate
3. F33.2 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent severe without psychotic features

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
- Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the treatment session was furnished.
- Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.

sections.heading: Implementation
sections.text: This policy applies to claims with dates of service on or after 09/01/2024.

sections.text:

Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with chronic refractory osteomyelitis.

- The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.

sections.heading: Limitations and Exclusions
sections.text:

Topical oxygen applied to the wound is not covered as hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Treatment for chronic peripheral vascular insufficiency alone is not covered.

sections.text: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is limited to 30 treatments within a 45-day period.

sections.heading: Covered Indications
sections.text:
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features. Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder. Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with treatment-resistant depression who cannot tolerate medication.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
sections.text:
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of major depressive disorder. The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care. The beneficary has not responded to at least 2 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.

sections.heading: Non-Covered Services
sections.text:
The following limitations apply:
- Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered.
- Maintenance treatment after remission is not covered.
- Simultaneous treatment with electroconvulsive therapy is not covered.

sections.heading: Utilization Guidelines
sections.text: A course of treatment is limited to 42 sessions over 9 weeks.

sections.heading: Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
sections.text: Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 6 months before the initial treatment session must be available. A baseline result from a standardized depression rating scale must be recorded before the initial treatment session.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
sections.text:
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
- When transcranial magnetic stimulation continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.
- The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.
- Results of a standardized depression rating scale relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.
- The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for transcranial magnetic stimulation from the treating practitioner.

sections.heading: Provider Qualifications
sections.text:
- Staff furnishing transcranial magnetic stimulation must hold current basic life support certification.
- The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for transcranial magnetic stimulation:
1. F32.1 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
2. F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate
3. F33.2 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent severe without psychotic features

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
- Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.
- Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.
- Report one unit of service for each treatment session furnished.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence. Published studies report improvements in depression rating scale scores among beneficiaries receiving transcranial magnetic stimulation. Evidence for benefit is strongest when transcranial magnetic stimulation is combined with ongoing medical management.

sections.heading: Implementation
sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 04/01/2019.

sections.heading: References
sections.text:
- Example Journal of Psychiatry. Outcomes of transcranial magnetic stimulation in older adults. 2018.
- Fictional Society of Psychiatry. Clinical practice guideline for major depressive disorder. 2021 edition.

sections.text: Questions about this policy may be directed to the fictional contractor policy unit at policy-unit-67@example.org.

sections.heading: Limitations and Exclusions

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Covered Indications
This section describes the indications for which bone mass measurement may be covered.
1. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism.
2. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for estrogen-deficient women at clinical risk for osteoporosis.
3. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture.
Eligibility Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
1. The beneficiary is at least 60 years of age.
2. The results will be used to guide treatment decisions.
3. The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
4. The ordering practitioner is treating the beneficiary for a condition that affects bone density.
Limitations
The following limitations apply:
1. Testing more often than the frequency limit is not covered without documented medical necessity.
2. Vertebral fracture assessment billed alone without a qualifying indication is not covered.
3. Peripheral bone density testing used only for screening is not covered.
Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry obtained within 6 months before the initial scan must be available.
Provider Qualifications
1. Facilities furnishing bone mass measurement must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
2. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in radiology.
3. Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform bone mass measurement under state law.
4. Bone mass measurement must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Utilization Guidelines
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 24 months.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The following documentation must be available upon request:
- The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about bone mass measurement.
- The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.
- Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each scan.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for bone mass measurement:
- E21.3 - Hyperparathyroidism, unspecified
- E28.310 - Symptomatic premature menopause
- M81.0 - Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
- Z87.310 - Personal history of (healed) osteoporosis fracture

sections.text:
Covered Indications
This section describes the indications for which bone mass measurement may be covered.
1. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism.
2. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for estrogen-deficient women at clinical risk for osteoporosis.
3. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture.
Eligibility Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
1. The beneficiary is at least 60 years of age.
2. The results will be used to guide treatment decisions.
3. The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
4. The ordering practitioner is treating the beneficiary for a condition that affects bone density.
Limitations
The following limitations apply:
1. Testing more often than the frequency limit is not covered without documented medical necessity.
2. Vertebral fracture assessment billed alone without a qualifying indication is not covered.
3. Peripheral bone density testing used only for screening is not covered.
Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry obtained within 6 months before the initial scan must be available.
Provider Qualifications
1. Facilities furnishing bone mass measurement must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
2. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in radiology.
3. Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform bone mass measurement under state law.
4. Bone mass measurement must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Coverage Indications
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with decompression illness. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with osteoradionecrosis. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with acute carbon monoxide poisoning. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with compromised skin grafts or flaps.
Medical Necessity Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
The beneficiary has been evaluated for hyperbaric treatment by the supervising physician. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 30 days. The wound is classified as Wagner grade 2 or higher.
Limitations
The following limitations apply:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for beneficiaries with untreated pneumothorax. Topical oxygen applied to the wound is not covered as hyperbaric oxygen therapy.
Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
The following clinical evidence is required:
1. Results of transcutaneous oxygen measurement obtained within 3 months before the initial treatment must be available.
2. A baseline result from transcutaneous oxygen measurement must be recorded before the initial treatment.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The following qualifications apply:
Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform hyperbaric oxygen therapy under state law. The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare. Facilities furnishing hyperbaric oxygen therapy must maintain written protocols for emergency response.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Utilization Guidelines
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is limited to 20 treatments within a 45-day period.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
- Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each treatment.
- The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment.
- A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before hyperbaric oxygen therapy begins.
- Documentation must state the clinical reason any treatment was missed or discontinued.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
1. E11.621 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
2. M27.8 - Other specified diseases of jaws
3. T58.01XA - Toxic effect of carbon monoxide from motor vehicle exhaust, accidental (unintentional), initial encounter

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
- Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the treatment was furnished.
- Report one unit of service for each treatment furnished.
- Claims for hyperbaric oxygen therapy furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.
- Telehealth delivery of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not separately billable under this policy.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Published studies report improvements in wound healing and amputation rates among beneficiaries receiving hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence. Evidence for benefit is strongest when hyperbaric oxygen therapy is combined with ongoing medical management.

sections.heading: References
sections.text: Fictional Society of Undersea and Hyperbaric Medicine. Clinical practice guideline for hypoxic wounds and related conditions. 2022 edition.

sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder. Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder. Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with treatment-resistant depression who cannot tolerate medication.
Eligibility Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
1. A psychiatric evaluation has confirmed the diagnosis.
2. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 90 days.
3. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 1 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
Limitations
The following limitations apply:
Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered. Simultaneous treatment with electroconvulsive therapy is not covered. Maintenance treatment after remission is not covered.
Required Testing
1. Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 12 months before the initial treatment session must be available.
2. A baseline result from a standardized depression rating scale must be recorded before the initial treatment session.
Provider Qualifications
Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for major depressive disorder. Facilities furnishing transcranial magnetic stimulation must maintain written protocols for emergency response.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Utilization Guidelines
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
A course of treatment is limited to 36 sessions over 7 weeks.
Documentation Requirements
The following documentation must be available upon request:
- The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.
- The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about transcranial magnetic stimulation.
- Documentation must state the clinical reason any treatment session was missed or discontinued.
- The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for transcranial magnetic stimulation from the treating practitioner.
- A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before transcranial magnetic stimulation begins.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
Bone mass measurement is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries receiving long-term glucocorticoid therapy. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries with vertebral abnormalities on imaging. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries being monitored on an FDA-approved osteoporosis medication.
Medical Necessity Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
- The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
- The beneficiary is at least 60 years of age.
- The results will be used to guide treatment decisions.
Non-Covered Services
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
Testing more often than the frequency limit is not covered without documented medical necessity. Peripheral bone density testing used only for screening is not covered.
Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
The following clinical evidence is required:
Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry obtained within 18 months before the initial scan must be available.
Provider Qualifications
- The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare.
- The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in radiology.
- The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in bone mass measurement.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 23 months.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial scan. Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each. The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity. Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record. Documentation must state the clinical reason any scan was missed or discontinued.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
- M81.0 - Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
- Z79.52 - Long term (current) use of systemic steroids
- Z87.310 - Personal history of (healed) osteoporosis fracture

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Covered Indications
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.
Medical Necessity Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
1. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
2. The beneficiary is not at acute risk of suicide requiring inpatient care.
3. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 3 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
4. The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
Limitations
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
1. Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered.
2. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is not covered for beneficiaries with a seizure disorder.
3. Treatment delivered with devices not cleared for depression is not covered.
Provider Qualifications
1. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for major depressive disorder.
2. Staff furnishing transcranial magnetic stimulation must hold current basic life support certification.
3. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Documentation Requirements
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
1. Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each treatment session.
2. Documentation must state the clinical reason any treatment session was missed or discontinued.
3. A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before transcranial magnetic stimulation begins.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for transcranial magnetic stimulation:
- F32.2 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
- F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate
- F33.2 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent severe without psychotic features
- F33.9 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, unspecified

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
1. Report the date of the initial treatment session on the claim.
2. Report one unit of service for each treatment session furnished.
3. Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when transcranial magnetic stimulation is combined with ongoing medical management. The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies. Published studies report improvements in depression rating scale scores among beneficiaries receiving transcranial magnetic stimulation.

sections.heading: Applicability
sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 12/01/2025.

sections.heading: References
sections.text:
- Example Journal of Psychiatry. Outcomes of transcranial magnetic stimulation in older adults. 2020.
- Synthetic Evidence Review Group. Systematic review of transcranial magnetic stimulation outcomes. 2015.

sections.text: Questions about this policy may be directed to the fictional contractor policy unit at policy-unit-33@example.org.

sections.text:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.

sections.heading: Patient Selection Criteria
sections.text:
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
The wound is classified as Wagner grade 2 or higher. The beneficiary has been evaluated for hyperbaric treatment by the supervising physician. sections.heading: Limitations
sections.text:

sections.heading: Frequency and Duration
sections.text: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is limited to 20 treatments within a 30-day period.

- The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Coverage Indications
This section describes the indications for which hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered.
- Coverage of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is provided for beneficiaries with chronic refractory osteomyelitis.
- Coverage of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is provided for beneficiaries with diabetic lower extremity wounds.
- Coverage of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is provided for beneficiaries with acute carbon monoxide poisoning.
- Coverage of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is provided for beneficiaries with compromised skin grafts or flaps.
Patient Selection Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement. The wound is classified as Wagner grade 2 or higher. There is no untreated pneumothorax. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
Non-Covered Services
The following limitations apply:
Topical oxygen applied to the wound is not covered as hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Treatment for chronic peripheral vascular insufficiency alone is not covered. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for beneficiaries with untreated pneumothorax.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The following qualifications apply:
1. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for hypoxic wounds and related conditions.
2. The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare.
3. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is limited to 40 treatments within a 60-day period.
Documentation Requirements
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
1. When hyperbaric oxygen therapy continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.
2. Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each treatment.
3. The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
Transcranial magnetic stimulation is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
1. Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.
2. Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features.
3. Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.
Medical Necessity Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 60 days. The beneficiary is not at acute risk of suicide requiring inpatient care. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 2 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
Non-Covered Services
The following limitations apply:
- Treatment delivered with devices not cleared for depression is not covered.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation is not covered for beneficiaries with a seizure disorder.
- Simultaneous treatment with electroconvulsive therapy is not covered.
Required Testing
The following clinical evidence is required:
Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 3 months before the initial treatment session must be available.
Provider Qualifications
The following qualifications apply:
1. Facilities furnishing transcranial magnetic stimulation must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
2. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for major depressive disorder.
3. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
A course of treatment is limited to 30 sessions over 7 weeks.
Documentation Requirements
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each treatment session. Documentation must state the clinical reason any treatment session was missed or discontinued. A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before transcranial magnetic stimulation begins. Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each treatment session.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
- F32.2 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
- F33.2 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent severe without psychotic features
- F33.9 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, unspecified

sections.text: The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim. Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected. sections.text: The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies. Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence. Published studies report improvements in depression rating scale scores among beneficiaries receiving transcranial magnetic stimulation.

sections.heading: Indications for Coverage
sections.text:
This section describes the indications for which bone mass measurement may be covered.
1. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries receiving long-term glucocorticoid therapy.
2. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism.
3. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries being monitored on an FDA-approved osteoporosis medication.
4. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture.

sections.heading: Patient Selection Criteria
sections.text:
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
1. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
2. The beneficiary is at least 65 years of age.
3. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of osteoporosis.

sections.heading: Non-Covered Services
sections.text:
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
Peripheral bone density testing used only for screening is not covered. Testing more often than the frequency limit is not covered without documented medical necessity. Bone mass measurement is not covered for beneficiaries without a qualifying risk factor.

sections.heading: Frequency and Duration
sections.text:
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 18 months.

sections.heading: Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
sections.text:
The following clinical evidence is required:
Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry obtained within 6 months before the initial scan must be available.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
sections.text:
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each scan. Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each scan. A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before bone mass measurement begins. Documentation must state the clinical reason any scan was missed or discontinued. The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about bone mass measurement.

sections.heading: Provider Qualifications
sections.text:
- The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in radiology.
- Facilities furnishing bone mass measurement must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
- Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform bone mass measurement under state law.
- Bone mass measurement must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for bone mass measurement:
- E21.3 - Hyperparathyroidism, unspecified
- E28.310 - Symptomatic premature menopause
- Z79.52 - Long term (current) use of systemic steroids
- Z87.310 - Personal history of (healed) osteoporosis fracture

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
- Report the date of the initial scan on the claim.
- The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim.
- Report one unit of service for each scan furnished.
- Telehealth delivery of bone mass measurement is not separately billable under this policy.

sections.heading: References
sections.text: Example Journal of Radiology. Outcomes of bone mass measurement in older adults. 2019.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Coverage Indications
Transcranial magnetic stimulation is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
Medical Necessity Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
1. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of major depressive disorder.
2. The beneficiary has no implanted metallic device near the treatment coil.
3. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
4. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 1 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
Limitations
The following limitations apply:
1. Simultaneous treatment with electroconvulsive therapy is not covered.
2. Treatment delivered with devices not cleared for depression is not covered.
Provider Qualifications
Facilities furnishing transcranial magnetic stimulation must maintain written protocols for emergency response. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in psychiatry.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
A course of treatment is limited to 30 sessions over 6 weeks.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity. Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each treatment session. The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for transcranial magnetic stimulation from the treating practitioner. Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each treatment session.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
- F32.1 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
- F32.2 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
- F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
1. Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.
2. The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim.

sections.heading: Implementation
sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 06/01/2023.

sections.heading: References
sections.text:
- Synthetic Evidence Review Group. Systematic review of transcranial magnetic stimulation outcomes. 2015.
- Example Journal of Psychiatry. Outcomes of transcranial magnetic stimulation in older adults. 2012.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Covered Indications
This section describes the indications for which hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with decompression illness.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with acute carbon monoxide poisoning.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with diabetic lower extremity wounds.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with compromised skin grafts or flaps.
Patient Selection Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
- The wound has failed to respond to standard wound therapy for at least 30 days.
- The wound is classified as Wagner grade 2 or higher.
- The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
- The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
Limitations and Exclusions
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
- Treatment for chronic peripheral vascular insufficiency alone is not coverd.
- Treatment continued without measurable signs of healing after 30 days is not covered.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
- The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in hyperbaric oxygen therapy.
- Staff furnishing hyperbaric oxygen therapy must hold current basic life support certification.
- Facilities furnishing hyperbaric oxygen therapy must maintain written protocols for emergency response.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is limited to 20 treatments within a 60-day period.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Documentation must state the clinical reason any treatment was missed or discontinued. Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each. Results of transcutaneous oxygen measurement relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
- E11.621 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
- M27.8 - Other specified diseases of jaws
- T58.01XA - Toxic effect of carbon monoxide from motor vehicle exhaust, accidental (unintentional), initial encounter
- T70.3XXA - Caisson disease [decompression sickness], initial encounter

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
- The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim.
- Telehealth delivery of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not separately billable under this policy.
- Claims for hyperbaric oxygen therapy furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.
- Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence
sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when hyperbaric oxygen therapy is combined with ongoing medical management. Published studies report improvements in wound healing and amputation rates among beneficiaries receiving hyperbaric oxygen therapy.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text: Synthetic Evidence Review Group. Systematic review of hyperbaric oxygen therapy outcomes. 2021.

sections.text: Questions about this policy may be directed to the fictional contractor policy unit at policy-unit-42@example.org.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Covered Indications
This section describes the indications for which bone mass measurement may be covered.
Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries receiving long-term glucocorticoid therapy. Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries with vertebral abnormalities on imaging. Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture. Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for estrogen-deficient women at clinical risk for osteoporosis.
Patient Selection Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
- The ordering practitioner is treating the beneficiary for a condition that affects bone density.
- The results will be used to guide treatment decisions.
- The beneficiary is at least 65 years of age.
- The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 30 days.
Limitations and Exclusions
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
Testing more often than the frequency limit is not covered without documented medical necessity. Bone mass measurement is not covered when performed only to confirm a prior result from a different modality.
Provider Qualifications
- Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform bone mass measurement under state law.
- Bone mass measurement must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for osteoporosis.
- Staff furnishing bone mass measurement must hold current basic life support certification.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 18 months.
Documentation Requirements
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
1. Documentation must state the clinical reason any scan was missed or discontinued.
2. The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.
3. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial scan.
4. Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each scan.
5. Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
- M81.0 - Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
- Z79.52 - Long term (current) use of systemic steroids
- Z87.310 - Personal history of (healed) osteoporosis fracture

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
1. Report the date of the initial scan on the claim.
2. Report one unit of service for each scan furnished.
3. Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Published studies report improvements in fracture risk assessment among beneficiaries receiving bone mass measurement. The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies.

sections.heading: Implementation
sections.text: This policy applies to claims with dates of service on or after 12/01/2022.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text:
- Example Journal of Radiology. Outcomes of bone mass measurement in older adults. 2013.
- Synthetic Evidence Review Group. Systematic review of bone mass measurement outcomes. 2013.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications
sections.text:
Transcranial magnetic stimulation is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with treatment-resistant depression who cannot tolerate medication.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
sections.text:
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
1. The beneficiary has no implanted metallic device near the treatment coil.
2. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
3. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 4 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.

sections.heading: Limitations
sections.text:
The following limitations apply:
1. Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered.
2. Treatment delivered with devices not cleared for depression is not covered.
3. Maintenance treatment after remission is not covered.

sections.heading: Frequency and Duration
sections.text: A course of treatment is limited to 30 sessions over 7 weeks.

sections.heading: Required Testing
sections.text:
The following clinical evidence is required:
Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 3 months before the initial treatment session must be available.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
sections.text:
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before transcranial magnetic stimulation begins. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment session. Results of a standardized depression rating scale relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.

sections.heading: Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
sections.text:
1. Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform transcranial magnetic stimulation under state law.
2. Staff furnishing transcranial magnetic stimulation must hold current basic life support certification.
3. The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare.
4. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
1. F32.1 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
2. F32.2 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
3. F33.9 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, unspecified

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
- Telehealth delivery of transcranial magnetic stimulation is not separately billable under this policy.
- Claims for transcranial magnetic stimulation furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.
- The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence. Published studies report improvements in depression rating scale scores among beneficiaries receiving transcranial magnetic stimulation.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text: Example Journal of Psychiatry. Outcomes of transcranial magnetic stimulation in older adults. 2021.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Coverage Indications
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with acute carbon monoxide poisoning. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with compromised skin grafts or flaps. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with decompression illness. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with diabetic lower extremity wounds.
Eligibility Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
The wound is classified as Wagner grade 3 or higher. The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care. The wound has failed to respond to standard wound therapy for at least 30 days.
Limitations and Exclusions
The following limitations apply:
1. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for beneficiaries with untreated pneumothorax.
2. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for acute cerebral edema.
3. Treatment continued without measurable signs of healing after 30 days is not covered.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The following qualifications apply:
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for hypoxic wounds and related conditions.
- Staff furnishing hyperbaric oxygen therapy must hold current basic life support certification.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is limited to 40 treatments within a 30-day period.
Documentation Requirements
The following documentation must be available upon request:
- The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for hyperbaric oxygen therapy from the treating practitioner.
- Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each treatment.
- When hyperbaric oxygen therapy continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for hyperbaric oxygen therapy:
1. E11.621 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
2. M27.8 - Other specified diseases of jaws
3. T58.01XA - Toxic effect of carbon monoxide from motor vehicle exhaust, accidental (unintentional), initial encounter
4. T70.3XXA - Caisson disease [decompression sickness], initial encounter

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
- The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim.
- Report one unit of service for each treatment furnished.
- Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when hyperbaric oxygen therapy is combined with ongoing medical management. Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence. The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text: Example Journal of Undersea and Hyperbaric Medicine. Outcomes of hyperbaric oxygen therapy in older adults. 2018.

Indications for Coverage
Transcranial magnetic stimulation is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
1. Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with treatment-resistant depression who cannot tolerate medication.
2. Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features.
3. Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.
4. Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.
Eligibility Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
- Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement.
- The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
- The beneficiary has not responded to at least 1 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
Limitations
The following limitations apply:
Treatment delivered with devices not cleared for depression is not covered. Maintenance treatment after remission is not covered.
Required Testing
Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 18 months before the initial treatment session must be available. A baseline result from a standardized depression rating scale must be recorded before the initial treatment session.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
- Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform transcranial magnetic stimulation under state law.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for major depressive disorder.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

The following frequency and duration limits apply:

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with treatment-resistant depression who cannot tolerate medication.
Medical Necessity Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
The beneficiary has not responded to at least 3 adequate trials of antidepressant medication. The beneficiary is not at acute risk of suicide requiring inpatient care. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 90 days.
Limitations
The following limitations apply:
1. Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered.
2. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is not covered for beneficiaries with a seizure disorder.
Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
The following clinical evidence is required:
1. Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 18 months before the initial treatment session must be available.
2. A baseline result from a standardized depression rating scale must be recorded before the initial treatment session.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The following qualifications apply:
The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in psychiatry. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
A course of treatment is limited to 30 sessions over 9 weeks.
Documentation Requirements
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
When transcranial magnetic stimulation continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement. The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for transcranial magnetic stimulation from the treating practitioner. Results of a standardized depression rating scale relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:

1. F32.1 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
2. F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate
3. F33.2 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent severe without psychotic features

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the treatment session was furnished. The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim.

2. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
3. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 30 days.
Limitations

2. Vertebral fracture assessment billed alone without a qualifying indication is not covered.

Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry obtained within 12 months before the initial scan must be available.
Provider Qualifications
The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in radiology. Facilities furnishing bone mass measurement must maintain written protocols for emergency response. Bone mass measurement must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
