This section describes the indications for which hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with decompression illness.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with acute carbon monoxide poisoning.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with osteoradionecrosis.
Eligibility Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
- The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of hypoxic wounds and related conditions.
- Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement.
- The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 90 days.
- The wound is classified as Wagner grade 4 or higher.
Non-Covered Services
The following limitations apply:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for acute cerebral edema. Treatment for chronic peripheral vascular insufficiency alone is not covered.
Provider Qualifications
Staff furnishing hyperbaric oxygen therapy must hold current basic life support certification. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for hypoxic wounds and related conditions. The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in hyperbaric oxygen therapy.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:

Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is limited to 30 treatments within a 60-day period.
Documentation Requirements
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
- Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each treatment.
- Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each treatment.
- Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:

- T58.01XA - Toxic effect of carbon monoxide from motor vehicle exhaust, accidental (unintentional), initial encounter
- T70.3XXA - Caisson disease [decompression sickness], initial encounter

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
1. Report one unit of service for each treatment furnished.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when hyperbaric oxygen therapy is combined with ongoing medical management. Published studies report improvements in wound healing and amputation rates among beneficiaries receiving hyperbaric oxygen therapy.

sections.text: This policy applies to claims with dates of service on or after 10/01/2025.

sections.text: Fictional Society of Undersea and Hyperbaric Medicine. Clinical practice guideline for hypoxic wounds and related conditions. 2018 edition.

sections.text:
Coverage Indications
This section describes the indications for which hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with chronic refractory osteomyelitis.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with diabetic lower extremity wounds.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with decompression illness.
Eligibility Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
The wound is classified as Wagner grade 4 or higher. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period. Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement. The beneficiary has been evaluated for hyperbaric treatment by the supervising physician.
Non-Covered Services
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for beneficiaries with untreated pneumothorax.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for acute cerebral edema.
- Topical oxygen applied to the wound is not covered as hyperbaric oxygen therapy.
Provider Qualifications
The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in undersea and hyperbaric medicine. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for hypoxic wounds and related conditions. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

3. The ordering practitioner is treating the beneficiary for a condition that affects bone density.

- Peripheral bone density testing used only for screening is not covered.

- Staff furnishing bone mass measurement must hold current basic life support certification.

- Bone mass measurement must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
This section describes the indications for which hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered.
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with acute carbon monoxide poisoning. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with compromised skin grafts or flaps. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with diabetic lower extremity wounds.
Medical Necessity Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
1. The wound is classified as Wagner grade 3 or higher.
2. The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
3. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 90 days.
Non-Covered Services
The following limitations apply:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for acute cerebral edema. Topical oxygen applied to the wound is not covered as hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for beneficiaries with untreated pneumothorax.
Provider Qualifications
The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in undersea and hyperbaric medicine. Facilities furnishing hyperbaric oxygen therapy must maintain written protocols for emergency response. The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The following documentation must be available upon request:
1. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment.
2. A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before hyperbaric oxygen therapy begins.
3. The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for hyperbaric oxygen therapy from the treating practitioner.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
1. E11.621 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
2. M27.8 - Other specified diseases of jaws
3. T58.01XA - Toxic effect of carbon monoxide from motor vehicle exhaust, accidental (unintentional), initial encounter
4. T70.3XXA - Caisson disease [decompression sickness], initial encounter

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
- Report one unit of service for each treatment furnished.
- Report the date of the initial treatment on the claim.
- Telehealth delivery of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not separately billable under this policy.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when hyperbaric oxygen therapy is combined with ongoing medical management. Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence. The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies.

sections.heading: References
sections.text: Synthetic Evidence Review Group. Systematic review of hyperbaric oxygen therapy outcomes. 2018.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
This section describes the indications for which bone mass measurement may be covered.
- Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries with vertebral abnormalities on imaging.
- Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries being monitored on an FDA-approved osteoporosis medication.
- Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries receiving long-term glucocorticoid therapy.
- Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism.
Eligibility Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
1. Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement.
2. The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
3. The beneficiary is at least 50 years of age.
Non-Covered Services
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
- Bone mass measurement is not covered for beneficiaries without a qualifying risk factor.
- Testing more often than the frequency limit is not covered without documented medical necessity.
- Vertebral fracture assessment billed alone without a qualifying indication is not covered.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The following qualifications apply:
- The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in bone mass measurement.
- Bone mass measurement must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for osteoporosis.
- Bone mass measurement must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Utilization Guidelines
Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 24 months.
Documentation Requirements
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each scan. The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about bone mass measurement. Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each scan. Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)

1. E21.3 - Hyperparathyroidism, unspecified

3. Z79.52 - Long term (current) use of systemic steroids

sections.text: Telehealth delivery of bone mass measurement is not separately billable under this policy. Report one unit of service for each scan furnished. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the scan was furnished.

sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 03/01/2021.

Eligibility Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
- The results will be used to guide treatment decisions.
- The beneficiary is at least 60 years of age.
- The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
- The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 30 days.
Limitations and Exclusions
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:

Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The following qualifications apply:
The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare. Staff furnishing bone mass measurement must hold current basic life support certification. Bone mass measurement must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for osteoporosis. Bone mass measurement must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Medical Necessity Criteria
sections.text:
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
The results will be used to guide treatment decisions. The beneficiary is at least 60 years of age. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.

sections.heading: Limitations and Exclusions

sections.heading: Covered Indications
sections.text:
Transcranial magnetic stimulation is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered for beneficiaries with treatment-resistant depression who cannot tolerate medication.

sections.heading: Patient Selection Criteria
sections.text:
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
1. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 1 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
2. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of major depressive disorder.
3. The beneficiary has no implanted metallic device near the treatment coil.

sections.heading: Limitations and Exclusions
sections.text:
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
Simultaneous treatment with electroconvulsive therapy is not covered. Treatment delivered with devices not cleared for depression is not covered.

sections.heading: Required Testing
sections.text: Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 6 months before the initial treatment session must be available.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
sections.text:
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
- Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each treatment session.
- A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before transcranial magnetic stimulation begins.
- The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment session.

sections.heading: Provider Qualifications
sections.text:
The following qualifications apply:
1. Staff furnishing transcranial magnetic stimulation must hold current basic life support certification.
2. The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in transcranial magnetic stimulation.
3. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for transcranial magnetic stimulation:
1. F32.1 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
2. F32.2 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
3. F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate
4. F33.2 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent severe without psychotic features

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
1. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the treatment session was furnished.
2. Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.
3. Report the date of the initial treatment session on the claim.
4. Report one unit of service for each treatment session furnished.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence
sections.text: Published studies report improvements in depression rating scale scores among beneficiaries receiving transcranial magnetic stimulation. Evidence for benefit is strongest when transcranial magnetic stimulation is combined with ongoing medical management.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Covered Indications
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.
Eligibility Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 1 adequate trials of antidepressant medication. The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care. The beneficiary has no implanted metallic device near the treatment coil.
Limitations and Exclusions
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation is not covered for beneficiaries with a seizure disorder.
- Maintenance treatment after remission is not covered.
- Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
1. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for major depressive disorder.
2. The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in transcranial magnetic stimulation.
3. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
A course of treatment is limited to 30 sessions over 7 weeks.
Documentation Requirements
The following documentation must be available upon request:
The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment session. The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity. The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for transcranial magnetic stimulation from the treating practitioner. Results of a standardized depression rating scale relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
- F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate
- F33.2 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent severe without psychotic features
- F33.9 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, unspecified

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
- Claims for transcranial magnetic stimulation furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.
- Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.

sections.heading: Applicability
sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 03/01/2021.

sections.heading: References
sections.text:
- Example Journal of Psychiatry. Outcomes of transcranial magnetic stimulation in older adults. 2014.
- Synthetic Evidence Review Group. Systematic review of transcranial magnetic stimulation outcomes. 2020.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
Bone mass measurement is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
1. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture.
2. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism.
3. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries with vertebral abnormalities on imaging.
4. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries receiving long-term glucocorticoid therapy.
Eligibility Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
The beneficiary is at least 65 years of age. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period. The ordering practitioner is treating the beneficiary for a condition that affects bone density.
Non-Covered Services
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
- Bone mass measurement is not covered when performed only to confirm a prior result from a different modality.
- Vertebral fracture assessment billed alone without a qualifying indication is not covered.
- Testing more often than the frequency limit is not covered without documented medical necessity.
Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
The following clinical evidence is required:
1. Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry obtained within 12 months before the initial scan must be available.
2. A baseline result from dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry must be recorded before the initial scan.
Provider Qualifications
1. Facilities furnishing bone mass measurement must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
2. Staff furnishing bone mass measurement must hold current basic life support certification.
3. Bone mass measurement must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
- Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each scan.
- The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for bone mass measurement from the treating practitioner.
- The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.
- The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial scan.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
1. E21.3 - Hyperparathyroidism, unspecified
2. E28.310 - Symptomatic premature menopause
3. Z87.310 - Personal history of (healed) osteoporosis fracture

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
1. Claims for bone mass measurement furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.
2. The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim.
3. Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.
4. Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence
sections.text: The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies. Evidence for benefit is strongest when bone mass measurement is combined with ongoing medical management. Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text: Example Journal of Radiology. Outcomes of bone mass measurement in older adults. 2017.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications
sections.text:
This section describes the indications for which hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with acute carbon monoxide poisoning.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with diabetic lower extremity wounds.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with osteoradionecrosis.

sections.heading: Patient Selection Criteria
sections.text:
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
1. The wound is classified as Wagner grade 2 or higher.
2. Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement.
3. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of hypoxic wounds and related conditions.

sections.heading: Limitations and Exclusions
sections.text:
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
1. Topical oxygen applied to the wound is not covered as hyperbaric oxygen therapy.
2. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for beneficiaries with untreated pneumothorax.

sections.heading: Frequency and Duration
sections.text: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is limited to 20 treatments within a 60-day period.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements
sections.text:
The following documentation must be available upon request:
1. When hyperbaric oxygen therapy continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.
2. The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.
3. The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about hyperbaric oxygen therapy.

sections.heading: Provider Qualifications
sections.text: Facilities furnishing hyperbaric oxygen therapy must maintain written protocols for emergency response. The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for hyperbaric oxygen therapy:
1. E10.621 - Type 1 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
2. E11.621 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
3. M27.8 - Other specified diseases of jaws
4. T58.01XA - Toxic effect of carbon monoxide from motor vehicle exhaust, accidental (unintentional), initial encounter

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
- Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the treatment was furnished.
- Claims for hyperbaric oxygen therapy furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.
- Report the date of the initial treatment on the claim.
- Telehealth delivery of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not separately billable under this policy.

sections.heading: Implementation
sections.text: This policy applies to claims with dates of service on or after 07/01/2022.

sections.text: Fictional Society of Undersea and Hyperbaric Medicine. Clinical practice guideline for hypoxic wounds and related conditions. 2022 edition.

sections.text: Inquiries may be submitted to the fictional contractor medical review department at (555) 0121-7891.

Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of osteoporosis. The beneficary is at least 50 years of age. The ordering practitioner is treating the beneficiary for a condition that affects bone density.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Coverage Indications
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with treatment-resistant depression who cannot tolerate medication.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
Eligibility Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
1. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of major depressive disorder.
2. A psychiatric evaluation has confirmed the diagnosis.
3. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 4 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
4. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
Non-Covered Services
The following limitations apply:
Maintenance treatment after remission is not covered. Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is not covered for beneficiaries with a seizure disorder.
Required Testing
The following clinical evidence is required:
Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 12 months before the initial treatment session must be available. Objective findings that confirm major depressive disorder must be documented by the treating practitioner.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
- The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in transcranial magnetic stimulation.
- The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in psychiatry.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for major depressive disorder.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
A course of treatment is limited to 42 sessions over 7 weeks.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The following documentation must be available upon request:
1. When transcranial magnetic stimulation continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.
2. A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before transcranial magnetic stimulation begins.
3. The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
- F32.1 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
- F32.2 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
- F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
1. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the treatment session was furnished.
2. Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.
3. Claims for transcranial magnetic stimulation furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.
4. Telehealth delivery of transcranial magnetic stimulation is not separately billable under this policy.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when transcranial magnetic stimulation is combined with ongoing medical management. The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies. Published studies report improvements in depression rating scale scores among beneficiaries receiving transcranial magnetic stimulation.

sections.text: Example Journal of Psychiatry. Outcomes of transcranial magnetic stimulation in older adults. 2015.

sections.text: Inquiries may be submitted to the fictional contractor medical review department at (555) 0118-7408.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
sections.text:

- The ordering practitioner is treating the beneficiary for a condition that affects bone density.
- The beneficiary is at least 60 years of age.
- The beneficiary has at least one documented risk factor for osteoporosis.

sections.heading: Non-Covered Services
sections.text:

- Testing more often than the frequency limit is not covered without documented medical necessity.

sections.heading: Frequency and Duration
sections.text:

sections.heading: Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
sections.text:

- Objective findings that confirm osteoporosis must be documented by the treating practitioner.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements
sections.text:

sections.heading: Provider Qualifications
sections.text:

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Coverage Indications
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with acute carbon monoxide poisoning.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with osteoradionecrosis.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with chronic refractory osteomyelitis.
Medical Necessity Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period. The wound is classified as Wagner grade 3 or higher. The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care. Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement.
Non-Covered Services
The following limitations apply:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for acute cerebral edema. Treatment for chronic peripheral vascular insufficiency alone is not covered.
Required Testing
1. Results of transcutaneous oxygen measurement obtained within 3 months before the initial treatment must be available.
2. A baseline result from transcutaneous oxygen measurement must be recorded before the initial treatment.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
- The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in undersea and hyperbaric medicine.
- Staff furnishing hyperbaric oxygen therapy must hold current basic life support certification.
- Facilities furnishing hyperbaric oxygen therapy must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Documentation Requirements
The following documentation must be available upon request:
1. Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each treatment.
2. A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before hyperbaric oxygen therapy begins.
3. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment.
4. When hyperbaric oxygen therapy continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.
5. Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
1. E10.621 - Type 1 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
2. M27.8 - Other specified diseases of jaws
3. T70.3XXA - Caisson disease [decompression sickness], initial encounter

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
1. Claims submitted without the ordering practioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.
2. Report the date of the initial treatment on the claim.
3. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the treatment was furnished.

sections.heading: Implementation
sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 09/01/2019.

sections.text: Synthetic Evidence Review Group. Systematic review of hyperbaric oxygen therapy outcomes. 2015.

sections.text: Inquiries may be submitted to the fictional contractor medical review department at (555) 0171-5092.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Covered Indications
Bone mass measurement is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism. Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries receiving long-term glucocorticoid therapy. Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries being monitored on an FDA-approved osteoporosis medication. Coverage of bone mass measurement is provided for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture.
Medical Necessity Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 90 days. Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement. The beneficiary is at least 50 years of age.
Limitations and Exclusions
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
- Testing more often than the frequency limit is not covered without documented medical necessity.
- Peripheral bone density testing used only for screening is not covered.
Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry obtained within 6 months before the initial scan must be available.
Provider Qualifications
Facilities furnishing bone mass measurement must maintain written protocols for emergency response. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in radiology. Bone mass measurement must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Utilization Guidelines
Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 24 months.
Documentation Requirements
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
- The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for bone mass measurement from the treating practitioner.
- Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.
- A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before bone mass measurement begins.
- Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.
- The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial scan.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
- M81.0 - Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
- Z79.52 - Long term (current) use of systemic steroids
- Z87.310 - Personal history of (healed) osteoporosis fracture

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the scan was furnished. Report the date of the initial scan on the claim. Claims for bone mass measurement furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when bone mass measurement is combined with ongoing medical management. Published studies report improvements in fracture risk assessment among beneficiaries receiving bone mass measurement. Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence.

sections.heading: Implementation
sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 01/01/2025.

sections.heading: References
sections.text: Fictional Society of Radiology. Clinical practice guideline for osteoporosis. 2021 edition.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Coverage Indications
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
1. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.
2. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
3. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features.
Patient Selection Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
- The beneficiary has no implanted metallic device near the treatment coil.
- The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
- A psychiatric evaluation has confirmed the diagnosis.
- The beneficiary has not responded to at least 1 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
Non-Covered Services
The following limitations apply:
- Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered.
- Simultaneous treatment with electroconvulsive therapy is not covered.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
1. Staff furnishing transcranial magnetic stimulation must hold current basic life support certification.
2. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in psychiatry.
3. The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in transcranial magnetic stimulation.
4. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
A course of treatment is limited to 30 sessions over 6 weeks.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
1. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment session.
2. Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each treatment session.
3. The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for transcranial magnetic stimulation:
1. F32.1 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
2. F32.2 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
3. F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate
4. F33.2 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent severe without psychotic features

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
Report the date of the initial treatment session on the claim. Claims for transcranial magnetic stimulation furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence
sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when transcranial magnetic stimulation is combined with ongoing medical management. Published studies report improvements in depression rating scale scores among beneficiaries receiving transcranial magnetic stimulation. Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text: Synthetic Evidence Review Group. Systematic review of transcranial magnetic stimulation outcomes. 2015.

Non-Covered Services

- Transcranial magnetic stimulation is not covered for beneficiaries with a seizure disorder.
Provider Qualifications
The following qualifications apply:
1. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in psychiatry.
2. Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform transcranial magnetic stimulation under state law.

The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for transcranial magnetic stimulation from the treating practitioner. Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each treatment session.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Covered Indications
This section describes the indications for which bone mass measurement may be covered.
1. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries being monitored on an FDA-approved osteoporosis medication.
2. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries receiving long-term glucocorticoid therapy.
3. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism.
4. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture.
Eligibility Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
1. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
2. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 60 days.
3. The beneficiary is at least 50 years of age.
Limitations
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
- Bone mass measurement is not covered for beneficiaries without a qualifying risk factor.
- Testing more often than the frequency limit is not covered without documented medical necessity.
Required Testing
Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry obtained within 12 months before the initial scan must be available.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The following qualifications apply:
- Facilities furnishing bone mass measurement must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
- The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 23 months.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial scan. Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each. The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about bone mass measurement. The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity. A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before bone mass measurement begins.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for bone mass measurement:
1. E21.3 - Hyperparathyroidism, unspecified
2. E28.310 - Symptomatic premature menopause
3. M81.0 - Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
4. Z79.52 - Long term (current) use of systemic steroids

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text: Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected. Report the date of the initial scan on the claim. Telehealth delivery of bone mass measurement is not separately billable under this policy.

sections.heading: Implementation
sections.text: This policy applies to claims with dates of service on or after 03/01/2025.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text: Example Journal of Radiology. Outcomes of bone mass measurement in older adults. 2012.

sections.heading: Indications for Coverage
sections.text:
This section describes the indications for which bone mass measurement may be covered.
Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries being monitored on an FDA-approved osteoporosis medication. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture.

sections.heading: Patient Selection Criteria
sections.text:
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
- The ordering practitioner is treating the beneficiary for a condition that affects bone density.
- The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 90 days.
- The beneficiary is at least 65 years of age.

sections.heading: Non-Covered Services
sections.text:
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
1. Bone mass measurement is not covered when performed only to confirm a prior result from a different modality.
2. Bone mass measurement is not covered for beneficiaries without a qualifying risk factor.

sections.heading: Utilization Guidelines
sections.text:
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 18 months.

sections.heading: Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
sections.text:
The following clinical evidence is required:
1. Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry obtained within 3 months before the initial scan must be available.
2. Objective findings that confirm osteoporosis must be documented by the treating practitioner.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
sections.text:
The following documentation must be available upon request:
- The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.
- Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.
- The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for bone mass measurement from the treating practitioner.
- The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial scan.
- Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each scan.

sections.heading: Provider Qualifications
sections.text:
The following qualifications apply:
Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform bone mass measurement under state law. Facilities furnishing bone mass measurement must maintain written protocols for emergency response. Bone mass measurement must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for bone mass measurement:
1. E21.3 - Hyperparathyroidism, unspecified
2. E28.310 - Symptomatic premature menopause
3. M81.0 - Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
4. Z79.52 - Long term (current) use of systemic steroids

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text: Report one unit of service for each scan furnished. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the scan was furnished.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence
sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when bone mass measurement is combined with ongoing medical management. Published studies report improvements in fracture risk assessment among beneficiaries receiving bone mass measurement.

sections.heading: Applicability
sections.text: This policy applies to claims with dates of service on or after 09/01/2020.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text:
- Synthetic Evidence Review Group. Systematic review of bone mass measurement outcomes. 2021.
- Fictional Society of Radiology. Clinical practice guideline for osteoporosis. 2020 edition.

sections.heading: Frequency and Duration

This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
1. Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
2. Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features.
3. Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.
4. Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.
Medical Necessity Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
1. The beneficiary is not at acute risk of suicide requiring inpatient care.
2. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
3. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 60 days.
4. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 4 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
Limitations and Exclusions

Provider Qualifications

- The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare.
- Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform transcranial magnetic stimulation under state law.

sections.text:

sections.text:

sections.heading: Limitations and Exclusions
sections.text:

sections.heading: Frequency and Duration
sections.text:

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Coverage Indications
This section describes the indications for which bone mass measurement may be covered.
Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries being monitored on an FDA-approved osteoporosis medication. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries with vertebral abnormalities on imaging.
Medical Necessity Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
The beneficiary is at least 60 years of age. The ordering practitioner is treating the beneficiary for a condition that affects bone density. The beneficiary has at least one documented risk factor for osteoporosis.
Limitations
The following limitations apply:
1. Bone mass measurement is not covered for beneficiaries without a qualifying risk factor.
2. Vertebral fracture assessment billed alone without a qualifying indication is not covered.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The following qualifications apply:
1. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in radiology.
2. Staff furnishing bone mass measurement must hold current basic life support certification.
3. Bone mass measurement must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 18 months.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The following documentation must be available upon request:
Documentation must state the clinical reason any scan was missed or discontinued. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial scan. Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for bone mass measurement:
1. E21.3 - Hyperparathyroidism, unspecified
2. E28.310 - Symptomatic premature menopause
3. M81.0 - Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
4. Z87.310 - Personal history of (healed) osteoporosis fracture

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
- Report one unit of service for each scan furnished.
- Report the date of the initial scan on the claim.
- Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.
- Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the scan was furnished.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence
sections.text: Published studies report improvements in fracture risk assessment among beneficiaries receiving bone mass measurement. sections.heading: Covered Indications
sections.text:
Transcranial magnetic stimulation is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.

- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with treatment-resistant depression who cannot tolerate medication.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
sections.text:
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
- The beneficiary has not responded to at least 4 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
- A psychiatric evaluation has confirmed the diagnosis.
- The beneficiary has no implanted metallic device near the treatment coil.

sections.heading: Limitations and Exclusions
sections.text:
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered. Maintenance treatment after remission is not covered.

sections.text: A course of treatment is limited to 36 sessions over 7 weeks.

sections.heading: Required Testing
sections.text: Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 6 months before the initial treatment session must be available. Objective findings that confirm major depressive disorder must be documented by the treating practitioner.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements
sections.text:
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each. The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity. A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before transcranial magnetic stimulation begins.

sections.heading: Provider Qualifications
sections.text:
- The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in psychiatry.
- Staff furnishing transcranial magnetic stimulation must hold current basic life support certification.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for major depressive disorder.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:

The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
- E21.3 - Hyperparathyroidism, unspecified
- E28.310 - Symptomatic premature menopause
- Z79.52 - Long term (current) use of systemic steroids
- Z87.310 - Personal history of (healed) osteoporosis fracture

sections.heading: Billing Instructions

sections.text:

Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with vertebral abnormalities on imaging. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture. Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries receiving long-term glucocorticoid therapy.
Patient Selection Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
- The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 90 days.
- The results will be used to guide treatment decisions.
- The beneficiary is at least 65 years of age.
Non-Covered Services
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:

Required Testing
Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry obtained within 12 months before the initial scan must be available.
Provider Qualifications
- The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in radiology.
- Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform bone mass measurement under state law.
- Bone mass measurement must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:

- Documentation must state the clinical reason any scan was missed or discontinued.

- Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.
- A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before bone mass measurement begins.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications
sections.text:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with chronic refractory osteomyelitis.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with decompression illness.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with compromised skin grafts or flaps.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered for beneficiaries with osteoradionecrosis.

sections.heading: Patient Selection Criteria
sections.text:
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
The beneficiary has been evaluated for hyperbaric treatment by the supervising physician. The wound has failed to respond to standard wound therapy for at least 30 days. The wound is classified as Wagner grade 3 or higher. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 90 days.

sections.heading: Limitations and Exclusions
sections.text:
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for acute cerebral edema.
- Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is not covered for beneficiaries with untreated pneumothorax.

sections.heading: Frequency and Duration
sections.text: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is limited to 20 treatments within a 45-day period.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements
sections.text:
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
- A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before hyperbaric oxygen therapy begins.
- Results of transcutaneous oxygen measurement relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.
- The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment.
- Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.
- Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each treatment.

sections.heading: Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
sections.text:
1. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for hypoxic wounds and related conditions.
2. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in undersea and hyperbaric medicine.
3. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
1. E10.621 - Type 1 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
2. E11.621 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
3. M27.8 - Other specified diseases of jaws

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text: Report one unit of service for each treatment furnished. Report the date of the initial treatment on the claim. The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim. Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.

sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when hyperbaric oxygen therapy is combined with ongoing medical management. sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Coverage Indications
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with treatment-resistant depression who cannot tolerate medication.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features.
- Transcranial magnetic stimulation is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
Medical Necessity Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
1. The beneficiary has not responded to at least 1 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
2. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
3. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of major depressive disorder.
4. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 90 days.
Limitations and Exclusions
The following limitations apply:
Treatment delivered with devices not cleared for depression is not covered. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is not covered for beneficiaries with a seizure disorder.
Required Testing
Results of a standardized depression rating scale obtained within 12 months before the initial treatment session must be available.
Provider Qualifications
1. The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare.
2. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for major depressive disorder.
3. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The following documentation must be available upon request:
- When transcranial magnetic stimulation continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.
- Documentation must state the clinical reason any treatment session was missed or discontinued.
- Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.
- Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each treatment session.
- Results of a standardized depression rating scale relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for transcranial magnetic stimulation:
1. F32.1 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
2. F32.2 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
3. F33.2 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent severe without psychotic features
4. F33.9 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, unspecified

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
- Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.
- Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.
- Claims for transcranial magnetic stimulation furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.
- The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when transcranial magnetic stimulation is combined with ongoing medical management. Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence. The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies.

sections.heading: References
sections.text:
- Example Journal of Psychiatry. Outcomes of transcranial magnetic stimulation in older adults. 2016.
- Synthetic Evidence Review Group. Systematic review of transcranial magnetic stimulation outcomes. 2020.

sections.text: Questions about this policy may be directed to the fictional contractor policy unit at policy-unit-38@example.org.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Covered Indications
This section describes the indications for which bone mass measurement may be covered.
1. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture.
2. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism.
3. Bone mass measurement may be covered for beneficiaries receiving long-term glucocorticoid therapy.
Medical Necessity Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 30 days. The beneficiary is at least 60 years of age. The ordering practitioner is treating the beneficiary for a condition that affects bone density.
Non-Covered Services
The following limitations apply:
1. Bone mass measurement is not covered when performed only to confirm a prior result from a different modality.
2. Peripheral bone density testing used only for screening is not covered.
Provider Qualifications
The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare. Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform bone mass measurement under state law. Bone mass measurement must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for osteoporosis.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Utilization Guidelines
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 18 months.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The following documentation must be available upon request:
A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before bone mass measurement begins. Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record. The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for bone mass measurement from the treating practitioner. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial scan. Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for bone mass measurement:
1. E21.3 - Hyperparathyroidism, unspecified
2. E28.310 - Symptomatic premature menopause
3. Z87.310 - Personal history of (healed) osteoporosis fracture

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
- The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim.
- Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications
sections.text:
This section describes the indications for which transcranial magnetic stimulation may be covered.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with depressive episodes of bipolar disorder.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with major depressive disorder without psychotic features.
- Coverage of transcranial magnetic stimulation is provided for beneficiaries with recurrent depression who previously responded to transcranial magnetic stimulation.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
sections.text:
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
- The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
- The beneficiary has not responded to at least 1 adequate trials of antidepressant medication.
- The beneficiary has no implanted metallic device near the treatment coil.
- A psychiatric evaluation has confirmed the diagnosis.

sections.heading: Non-Covered Services
sections.text:
The following limitations apply:
1. Maintenance treatment after remission is not covered.
2. Treatment for depression with psychotic features is not covered.
3. Transcranial magnetic stimulation is not covered for beneficiaries with a seizure disorder.

sections.heading: Frequency and Duration
sections.text: A course of treatment is limited to 36 sessions over 6 weeks.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
sections.text:
The following documentation must be available upon request:
1. Documentation must state the clinical reason any treatment session was missed or discontinued.
2. Results of a standardized depression rating scale relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.
3. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment session.
4. Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each treatment session.
5. The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for transcranial magnetic stimulation from the treating practitioner.

sections.heading: Provider Qualifications
sections.text:
1. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for major depressive disorder.
2. The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare.
3. Transcranial magnetic stimulation must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for transcranial magnetic stimulation:
- F32.1 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate
- F32.2 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe without psychotic features
- F33.1 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate
- F33.9 - Major depressive disorder, recurrent, unspecified

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
1. Report one unit of service for each treatment session furnished.
2. Claims for transcranial magnetic stimulation furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Published studies report improvements in depression rating scale scores among beneficiaries receiving transcranial magnetic stimulation. The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies. Evidence for benefit is strongest when transcranial magnetic stimulation is combined with ongoing medical management.

sections.text: Fictional Society of Psychiatry. Clinical practice guideline for major depressive disorder. 2022 edition.

sections.text: Questions about this policy may be directed to the fictional contractor policy unit at policy-unit-93@example.org.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Covered Indications
This section describes the indications for which bone mass measurement may be covered.
- Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture.
- Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries being monitored on an FDA-approved osteoporosis medication.
- Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for estrogen-deficient women at clinical risk for osteoporosis.
Eligibility Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
- The beneficiary has at least one documented risk factor for osteoporosis.
- The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
- The beneficiary is at least 65 years of age.
- The ordering practitioner is treating the beneficiary for a condition that affects bone density.
Limitations and Exclusions
The following limitations apply:
Bone mass measurement is limited to 10 scans under this policy. Bone mass measurement is not covered when performed only to confirm a prior result from a different modality. Peripheral bone density testing used only for screening is not covered. Bone mass measurement is not covered for beneficiaries without a qualifying risk factor.
Provider Qualifications
The following qualifications apply:
1. Bone mass measurement must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for osteoporosis.
2. Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform bone mass measurement under state law.
3. The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in bone mass measurement.
4. Bone mass measurement must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Utilization Guidelines
Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 23 months.
Documentation Requirements
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
1. Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each scan.
2. When bone mass measurement continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.
3. Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each scan.
4. Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.
5. A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before bone mass measurement begins.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for bone mass measurement:
- E28.310 - Symptomatic premature menopause
- M81.0 - Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
- Z79.52 - Long term (current) use of systemic steroids
- Z87.310 - Personal history of (healed) osteoporosis fracture

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
This section describes the indications for which hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be covered.
1. Coverage of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is provided for beneficiaries with osteoradionecrosis.
2. Coverage of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is provided for beneficiaries with compromised skin grafts or flaps.
3. Coverage of hyperbaric oxygen therapy is provided for beneficiaries with diabetic lower extremity wounds.
Eligibility Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
- There is no untreated pneumothorax.
- The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
- The wound is classified as Wagner grade 3 or higher.
Limitations
The following limitations apply:
1. Topical oxygen applied to the wound is not covered as hyperbaric oxygen therapy.
2. Treatment continued without measurable signs of healing after 30 days is not covered.
Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
Results of transcutaneous oxygen measurement obtained within 12 months before the initial treatment must be available. Objective findings that confirm hypoxic wounds and related conditions must be documented by the treating practitioner.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
The following qualifications apply:
The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in undersea and hyperbaric medicine. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for hypoxic wounds and related conditions. Staff furnishing hyperbaric oxygen therapy must hold current basic life support certification.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy is limited to 20 treatments within a 30-day period.
Documentation Requirements
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
1. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial treatment.
2. Documentation must state the clinical reason any treatment was missed or discontinued.
3. The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
1. E10.621 - Type 1 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
2. M27.8 - Other specified diseases of jaws
3. T58.01XA - Toxic effect of carbon monoxide from motor vehicle exhaust, accidental (unintentional), initial encounter
4. T70.3XXA - Caisson disease [decompression sickness], initial encounter

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
1. Report one unit of service for each treatment furnished.
2. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the treatment was furnished.
3. Claims for hyperbaric oxygen therapy furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Published studies report improvements in wound healing and amputation rates among beneficiaries receiving hyperbaric oxygen therapy. The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text:
- Example Journal of Undersea and Hyperbaric Medicine. Outcomes of hyperbaric oxygen therapy in older adults. 2018.
- Synthetic Evidence Review Group. Systematic review of hyperbaric oxygen therapy outcomes. 2019.
